properties.decision:
Recorded as BRAINSTORMING, not as a proposal — the cement measurement (dec:idea-cement-is-measured-as-the-decision-layers-a-change-must-unpeel) given a weighting from Anthony's acquisitions training. Anthony, 2026-09-06, in his words: "this is also a 'sunk cost' type measurement. this reminded me of some of my air force acquisitions training: the Cost of Change Curve (often referred to in Defense Acquisition University / systems engineering training as the 'Rule of Tens' or the 'Cost Escalation Curve') … the cost to fix an error or implement a design change increases exponentially with each progressive phase of the system lifecycle … Locked-In Costs: early in the design phase actual spending is very low (10–15% of the budget) but the decisions made at this stage commit roughly 70–80% of the system's total life cycle cost … conceptual 1x, detailed design 3–6x, development and integration testing 10x, operations / fielded 100–1000x … once a satellite is launched, hardware is completely unalterable." Sources he cited: NASA SE Handbook 2.5 (cost-effectiveness considerations), NTRS 20100036670, DAU training.

THE MAPPING, and it is already in the graph: reflow2 records each node's lifecycle phase STRUCTURALLY — the phase-coverage detectors (concept_without_design, design_without_build, build_without_verification, no_deploy_operate) already walk it. For a Capability: no allocation = concept (1x); ALLOCATED_TO = designed (3–6x); an Artifact REALIZES it = built; a passing Verification = tested (10x); a realizing artifact INCLUDES-d in a deployed Release = fielded (100x+). A Requirement takes the furthest phase of what satisfies it. Unlike the decision-layer count, this reads NON-ZERO today, because realization and release edges are the edges this design actually draws.

⭐ WHAT IT READS ON THE EXPORT (2026-09-06): 231 Capabilities — 85 designed, 0 built-not-fielded, 0 tested-not-fielded, 146 fielded. 144 accepted Requirements — 8 concept, 29 designed, 107 fielded. All 286 registered Artifacts are in a deployed Release (release_includes_all ships everything, so nothing sits in the 10x tier here). Phase-weighted cost-to-change mass in the fielded tier: 98%. In DAU terms reflow2 is a FIELDED SYSTEM and every change to what exists is a 100x change by the curve; the 85 designed-but-unbuilt capabilities are the perimeter at 3x, which is where Anthony says the work now is, and the curve agrees that is where change is cheap.

⭐ AND THE FIELDED TIER OF reflow2 IS THE SCHEMA. The k-core measurement on the sibling idea found the cement is the eleven schema files and the core modules (k=5, 93 nodes). The curve says why: a satellite cannot be reached after launch, and a schema cannot be reached after it is deployed inside other people's design graphs — fact:defect-a-schema-narrowing-orphaned-live-edges-and-no-export-is-ever-imported is the retrofit cost paid once already. The decisions that fixed the schema were the July ones: dated decision authorship reads 43 in 2026-07, 345 in 2026-08, 15 in 2026-09 — 11% of the decisions, made when spending was smallest, holding the part that costs most to move. Whether those 43 govern the k=5 core is NOT measured here; it is the locked-in-cost claim and it is checkable.

THE FRAMINGS:
(a) BUILD THE PHASE-WEIGHTED READING — per node: furthest phase reached by its realization closure, times the curve; design-wide: the mass per tier. Cheap: the phase walk exists in detect.rs; the weights are a table. Counter-argument: the weights are hardware's. Mike Cohn's post — which Anthony himself cited — argues the curve is OUTDATED for software under continuous delivery, and reflow2 is that: 1,960 tests, a coherence gate, a one-word update, releases every few days, and a measured reversal rate of ~5% of accepted intent in seven weeks at no visible 100x cost. Where the curve DOES bite is the schema, because its retrofit is in other people's data, not in this repository.
(b) TWO CURVES, NOT ONE — code changes on this repo follow the flat software curve; schema and vocabulary changes follow the hardware curve because they are fielded in every consumer's graph. The instrument should weight by WHERE the node is fielded (this repo vs. consumers' graphs), which the graph can read: an Artifact under schema/ versus under crates/. Counter-argument: that is a reflow2-specific reading of a general instrument; for a user's design the distinction is theirs to state, and reflow2 should not guess it — which is (c).
(c) THE WEIGHTS ARE THE USER'S TO DECLARE — a space program says 1000x for fielded; a web service says 2x. reflow2 reads the PHASE from structure and takes the multipliers from a declared cost model on the Project, refusing to weight until they are stated (req:defaults-do-not-assert). Counter-argument: another unstated field nobody fills; but the three-legs pattern is the known answer, and the detector that notices absence is one line.
(d) LOCKED-IN COST AS A REPORT — which early decisions govern the fielded tier; the share of the design's cost-to-change mass that rests on decisions made in the first N% of its life. Checkable today from AUTHORED_BY acted_at and the k-core, not yet done. Counter-argument: it is history, not a lever; it says where the cement came from, not what to do about it.

WHAT IS CHEAP: (a) with declared weights, (d) as a one-off measurement. WHAT IS EXPENSIVE: nothing here; the expensive thing is elsewhere — the deferred world-scoping the cement idea already names.
properties.name: OPEN — is "how hard is this to change" the Cost of Change Curve read off the graph — each node's cost weighted by the lifecycle phase its realization has reached — and is the fielded tier of reflow2 the schema, because it is deployed in other people's designs?
properties.rationale: A RANKING IS A FINDING, NOT A DECISION. This is the first of the evening's four brainstorms whose instrument reads true TODAY, because it walks realization and release edges rather than decision edges — 98% of reflow2's phase-weighted mass is fielded, and the perimeter Anthony describes is the 85 designed-but-unbuilt capabilities at 3x. Its honest limit is the weights: the rule of tens is a hardware curve, one of Anthony's own sources says so for software, and reflow2's measured reversal rate does not look like 100x. The finding that survives that objection is (b): reflow2 has two curves, and the schema follows the hardware one because it is fielded inside other people's graphs — which is exactly the set of nodes the k-core measurement called the cement. So "sunk cost" here has a precise address: the eleven schema files, fixed by the 43 July decisions, reachable only by a migration every consumer must run. If any of this earns a session it is (c), weights declared by the project and phase read from structure, because it is the general form and the three-legs pattern already says how to make an optional declaration reach a design. Anthony's call.
